claims.claim: Energy Fuels began construction in July on commercial heavy-rare-earth capacity at White Mesa, moving terbium/dysprosium work beyond pilot-only status.
The expansion is estimated at about $104M capex and is designed to enable simultaneous commercial rare-earth and uranium processing, with planned later capacity expansion.

risks.risk: Commercial heavy-REE scale-up still requires construction, commissioning, feedstock and customer qualification execution.

unknowns.unknown: Commercial yields, operating costs and ramp timing for Tb/Dy remain unproven.

claims.claim: Energy Fuels expected about 1.6M lb finished U3O8 by June 30, already within its 1.5-2.5M lb full-year 2026 production guidance range.
The heavy-REE construction plan materially advances the prior pilot thesis, but government financing support remains conditional and execution-dependent.

risks.risk: Conditional government financing is not equivalent to closed funding and commodity exposure remains material.

contradictions.contradiction: Technical and construction milestones materially improve execution evidence, but commercial-scale heavy-REE economics remain prospective.

unknowns.unknown: Final financing mix and commercial heavy-REE economics remain unknown.
